title: Per-token contextualizer — UX annotated notes & grooming
content:
Goal: propose a different way to present token-level cost and latency by surfacing token role, semantic groupings, and a scrubber-first timeline. This doc collects annotated wireframe ideas, interaction patterns, user test scenarios, and a groomed backlog with estimates.

Problem statement (quick): current token-breakdown panels list tokens as a flat series with per-token cost stacked in a bar. It’s accurate but noisy for long responses, and it’s hard to: 1) understand where cost is being incurred (system vs user vs model prose vs tool calls), 2) correlate spikes to specific prompt elements, and 3) preserve temporal context for streaming responses.

Proposal summary: "Per-token contextualizer" — a compact timeline + role-aware token ribbon that groups tokens by semantic role and shows cost/latency bands. Key differentiators:
- Role-aware grouping: tokens are tagged and visually grouped into roles (system prompt, user prompt, instruction, model-generation, tool-call, function-args, safety/redaction). Groups can be collapsed/expanded.
- Scrub & playhead timeline: timeline scrubber that moves across invocation time; hovering shows token text, token role badge, per-token cost, and latency contribution. Playback lets you watch a streaming reconstruction with corresponding cost accumulation.
- Stacked microbars: each token visual encodes cost (height) and latency (color intensity) — small legend toggle to switch to absolute vs normalized view.
- Semantic fold: the UI automatically folds low-impact tokens (common stop words, whitespace) into a compressed gutter but retains them for token-index accuracy on demand.
- Inline diffs: support comparing two invocations (A/B) by overlaying an alternate token ribbon (ghosted) so you can see where cost/latency diverge.

Annotated wireframe (high-level panels):
1) Left column: invocation metadata (model variant, pinned version, route, customer tier, request-id, timestamp). Small CTA: "open raw trace" -> opens full trace with logs.
2) Middle: Token ribbon + scrubber (primary canvas). Top: timeline with coarse latency histogram. Middle: token ribbon with grouped bands (colored by role). Bottom: cost accumulation line (per-token cumulative $). Play/pause scrub controls and keyboard shortcuts (left/right = step token, shift+left/right = 10-token jump).
3) Right column: detail inspector. On hover or scrub, show: token index, token text (with truncation + expand), token role, token cost delta, latency delta, probable reason tags (e.g., kv-cache-miss, quantized-op-slow), link to sample kernel selection used for that token. Also show a compact stacktrace of model runtime path (e.g., attention mode, kv cache hit/miss).
4) Bottom: quick-filters & lenses: drop-in filters (by role, by cost percent, by latency percent, by token regex) and saved-lenses (e.g., "top-10-cost-token-roles" or "safety-audit").

Micro-interactions & edge cases: 
- Hover latency: small 200ms debounce to avoid jitter while moving the scrub.
- Folding: collapse/expand animation preserves playhead position.
- Sampling: for very long responses, we sample and show compressed groups; user can switch to "full mode" to stream all tokens.
- Redaction flagging: tokens flagged for redaction appear with a shield icon and a red border — clicking shows redaction reason.

User testing scenarios (for research):
- Scenario A (engineer debugging cost): "Find the 3 tokens causing a 12% unit-cost increase compared to the control run." Task: use filters and scrubbing to find tokens. Success metrics: time to identify token(s), clicks to open detail.
- Scenario B (SRE investigating latency spike): "A single invocation hit a 2s outlier; find what happened." Task: use timeline histogram and token detail to identify kernel or kv-cache issue. Success metrics: accuracy in root cause, confidence rating.
- Scenario C (product comparing rollouts): "Compare recent canary vs baseline for hallucinatory tool calls." Task: overlay two ribbons and inspect function-call tokens.

Accessibility notes: color choices must have >4.5 contrast for role badges; keyboard-first scrubbing must be reliable (focus ring, ARIA labels for tokens); screen-reader should expose collapsed group summaries.

Grooming/backlog (prioritized):
- UI-3325: token ribbon base scaffold (react canvas + scrub) — 5 days — owner: Marco Velez.
- CON-1214: role-tagging heuristic (server-side enrichment pipeline) — 8 days — owner: Liam Chen — depends on INFR-8345.
- INFR-8345: telemetry change: emit per-token kv-cache hit/miss and kernel-id — 6 days — owner: infra team.
- FE-4110: inspector detail panel (design + API) — 4 days — owner: Priya.
- EVAL-210: sample A/B overlay UX (prototype) — 3 days — owner: research.
- UX-5581: semantic fold algorithm (client heuristics + sampling) — spike 2 days then 4 dev days.

Open questions / unresolved trade-offs:
1) Where to compute token roles? Server enrich or client inference? Doing it server-side reduces client complexity but increases telemetry payload size.
2) Cost privacy: exposing raw per-token cost to support staff — do we mask micro-costs for customer-facing views? (compliance/legal).
3) Performance: rendering 10k tokens in the ribbon — need efficient canvas rendering + virtualized groups. Consider using WebGL for large traces.
4) Time series alignment for streaming vs batched invocations: should playhead step by token emission time or token index? UX preference test required.

Next steps (this sprint):
- Kickoff infra ticket INFR-8345; get telemetry schema finalized (owner: Liam).
- Spike: implement minimal ribbon scaffold (UI-3325) with mock data; user test with 4 internal engineers next week.
- Design: hi-fi wireframe for inspector and role badges (Priya).
- Legal: quick check on cost masking policy (ask Jenn in finance).

Notes to self / rough sketches:
- Consider green/yellow/red banding based on percentile buckets rather than absolute thresholds (percentile across customer baseline).
- "Pin token" feature: allow users to pin tokens to compare across invocations (persisted in route view).
- Saved-lens presets should be shareable links to reproduce a filtering state.

Reference links and examples:
- existing token inspector ideas (see token-pathway-wireflow) for context — compare mental model.
- attach mock CSV with sample per-token events for the spike test (to be uploaded).

End of notes. Feedback requested: what role taxonomies are necessary for support vs customer-facing UX? Do we want per-token $ to be shown in micro-dollars or normalized units by default?
